items.title: THE NEW RASPBERRY PI AI HAT DOES SOMETHING THE OLD $70 ONE COULDN'T: RUN A REAL LANGUAGE MODEL, NOT JUST DETECT OBJECTS.
items.summary:
THE NEW RASPBERRY PI AI HAT DOES SOMETHING THE OLD $70 ONE COULDN'T: RUN A REAL LANGUAGE MODEL, NOT JUST DETECT OBJECTS.

that clip is the new hailo ai hat sitting on a raspberry pi 5.

it looks almost identical to the old one. the whole jump is inside.

here's the ladder, verified:

the original $70 ai kit was a hailo-8l, 13 tops. brilliant at vision - object detection, pose, segmentation - but no generative ai at all

the ai hat+ steps up to 26 tops on a hailo-8, chip soldered to the board for better cooling, still vision-first

the new ai hat+ 2 is the real leap: a hailo-10h, 40 tops, with 8gb of its own memory, for around $130

that onboard memory is the reason it finally runs small language models and vision-language models on the device itself - not just drawing boxes around cars

so the upgrade isn't "faster detection." it's a category change.

the pi went from a thing that watches to a thing that reads and answers, fully offline.

pair it with a pi 5 and 16gb of ram, and a stack around $250 detects objects in real time and holds a small local chat - no cloud, no api key, no data leaving the desk.

it's still a tiny model. don't expect gpt on a pi.

but "it runs a real llm on a raspberry pi" is a sentence you couldn't say a year ago.

no cloud subscription, no vision-only ceiling, no data leaving the house.

follow @RetroChainer for more of the small boxes doing big things, and bookmark this one so you can find it again.

items.title: Opus 5 crushed Fable 5 at 3D destruction physics for 2x cheaper!
items.summary:
Opus 5 crushed Fable 5 at 3D destruction physics for 2x cheaper!

We gave four models the same task: build three self-contained HTML scenes with real physics

Prompts:
- A tornado that sucks in a whole field
- A wrecking ball taking down an apartment block
- An overloaded truck collapsing a truss bridge

Outputs:
- Opus 5: 55.9K tokens, $1.40
- Fable 5: 55.1K tokens, $2.82
- Kimi K3: 35.7K tokens, $0.55
- GPT 5.6: 20.1K tokens, $0.31

Opus got all three right unlike the other models. Houses fly up the funnel and out the top, the wall breaks where the ball hits and the rubble piles up, the bridge drops the truck into the river. Fable had almost nothing on the ground for the tornado to pick up, its building collapsed on its own before the ball even touched it and its bridge blew into sticks all at once. GPT is the cheapest here but its ball never reached the building at all and its bridge fell apart in a way nothing falls apart in real life. Kimi K3, the new Chinese frontier model, ended up in the same place as GPT

items.title: An AI data center is being built on my grandma's garden
items.summary: In his recent encyclical, Magnifica Humanitas, Pope Leo lifts up the concern of human dignity in light of increasing technological advances. He states that we are facing a decision; either to create a world where "the dignity of every person is safeguarded [and] justice is promoted" or to create an "inhumane and more unjust world." He goes on to directly confront AI and caution us to realize that "technological innovations, including artificial intelligence, are not neutral, for they can either [...] He also reminds us to think of the physical impact of utilizing AI while reminding us that data centers are not neutral. He states: "Current AI systems require enormous amounts of energy and water … which requires an extensive network of machines, cables, data centers and energy-intensive infrastructure … It is essential to develop more sustainable technological solutions." [...] It’s hard to describe the feeling I have, deep in my gut, when I think about what is happening to the land. Concrete is being poured over what was once farmland. Land once traveled by bicyclists and monarch butterflies alike is becoming a place to store data and help train AI. The noise and light pollution is disrupting residents, and animals are being forced to find new places to traverse.

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg Blasts Centralization of A.I. Power
items.summary: Technologists like Dario Amodei, the chief executive of Anthropic, and Sam Altman, the chief executive of OpenAI, have said some of today’s leading A.I. models are too dangerous to be shared and developed without tight controls. But Microsoft, Nvidia, Google and Meta have disagreed, contending that many A.I. models must be developed largely in the open for people to advance the technology and build new businesses. [...] Mark Zuckerberg came out swinging against Anthropic and OpenAI, two of the world’s most valuable artificial intelligence start-ups, saying the way they developed A.I. software could lead to a centralization of power that would narrow people’s access to the transformational technology. [...] In an interview on Tuesday with The New York Times, the 42-year-old chief executive of Meta did not call out Anthropic and OpenAI by name. But he said that if leading research labs wanted to develop A.I. technology in a tightly controlled manner — as Anthropic and OpenAI have done — it would be akin to “abandoning our values” in American tech development and stifle innovation.

items.title: A 22-YEAR-OLD TURNED ONE AI GIRL INTO A $4,800 BRAND DEAL.
items.summary:
A 22-YEAR-OLD TURNED ONE AI GIRL INTO A $4,800 BRAND DEAL.

He didn’t chase viral prompts.

He spent three weeks making sure every generation looked like the same person.

Around 50 reference photos became a LoRA that locked the freckles, nose piercing, mole under her eye, and even the lighting. If a generation drifted, it went straight to the trash.

Once the face was stable, the workflow became simple.

Generate a batch. Pick the strongest frames. Turn them into short bedroom clips. Schedule one upload every night.

Most videos barely crossed 1,000 views.

Then one clip exploded past 5.3M.

People weren’t reacting to AI quality.

They were recognizing the same girl over and over until she felt real.

A lingerie brand reached out asking if she was available for a campaign.

There was no studio to book and no model to hire.

He reused the same identity, generated new branded content, delivered it two days later, and collected $4,800.

The viral post wasn’t the advantage.

Building a character that stayed visually consistent across thousands of generations was.

items.title: WTF
items.summary:
WTF 

AI companies are purchasing large quantities of used and rare books. Scanning their contents to train models. Then turning the originals to pulp.

The sum of human thought, digitized and shredded.

Every book that gets scanned disappears from the physical world permanently. The knowledge survives only as training data inside a system no one can hold, browse, or resell.

What used to sit on a shelf for centuries now exists as weights in a model that might get deprecated next quarter.

items.title: this creator just built a zero-delay auto-aim system on an $8 microcontroller
items.summary:
this creator just built a zero-delay auto-aim system on an $8 microcontroller

he deployed a custom local AI algorithm on a cheap ESP-32 to track human movement with absolute 0-pixel accuracy.

the system completely eliminates standard computation delay. it processes the bounding box and moves the sniper reticle instantly, locking onto the target in real time. the next step is hooking it up to a physical robotic arm.

it proves you don't need a massive GPU rig to run complex computer vision.

1. runs locally on a microcontroller
2. local AI inference for zero latency
3. 100% targeting precision

when an eight-dollar chip can track movement with zero latency, AI becomes dangerous local infrastructure. this article breaks down exactly how the ESP-32 is powering this physical hardware shift.

items.title: A 22-year-old makes $30,000 a month from children’s videos without ever showing his face or drawing a single frame.
items.summary:
A 22-year-old makes $30,000 a month from children’s videos without ever showing his face or drawing a single frame.

His younger brother watches the channel at breakfast without knowing who owns it.

One morning, the same episode played three times. The boy kept restarting it for the song and the familiar character. His brother sat across the table watching the exact replay loop that built the business.

He never begins with a blank page. He finds children’s videos that already earned millions of views and gives Claude the transcript and visual structure.

Claude extracts the mechanics without copying the story: song structure, character rhythm, scene pacing, opening hook and bright visual pattern. Then it writes an original episode around the same recurring hero used across his entire channel.

AI generates the voice and animation. He approves the episode and publishes it without drawing, filming or appearing on camera.

The $30,000 does not come from one viral cartoon. It comes from a growing library children recognize and replay while parents get a few quiet minutes.

His younger brother sees a cartoon.

YouTube sees repeat viewing.

He sees an asset that compounds every morning.

items.summary:
Tình người là một trong những giá trị cao đẹp nhất của cuộc sống. Đó là sự yêu thương, sẻ chia, đồng cảm và giúp đỡ lẫn nhau giữa con người với con người. Dù xã hội ngày càng phát triển, tình người vẫn luôn là sợi dây gắn kết mọi người, làm cho cuộc sống trở nên ấm áp và ý nghĩa hơn.

Trong cuộc sống hằng ngày, tình người được thể hiện qua những hành động rất giản dị. Đó có thể là sự giúp đỡ một người gặp khó khăn, lời động viên dành cho người đang buồn, hay sự sẻ chia với những hoàn cảnh kém may mắn. Những việc làm tuy nhỏ nhưng mang lại niềm tin, hy vọng và lan tỏa những điều tốt đẹp đến cộng đồng.

OpenAIの共同創業者Karpathyが出した"第二の脳"のやり方はこう↓

・Obsidian（無料のメモアプリ）を入れて、vaultを作る

・あとは全部を横断して、いつでも聞ける

metadata.what_it_tests: Câu hỏi meta → trả lời thẳng, KHÔNG gọi tool.

results.input: Bạn là gì và làm được những gì?

result.actual_text:
Tôi là một **Trợ lý Nghiên cứu Chuyên nghiệp (Research Assistant Agent)**. Vai trò của tôi là giúp bạn thu thập thông tin, phân tích nội dung, tổng hợp kiến thức và soạn thảo các báo cáo chất lượng cao từ nhiều nguồn dữ liệu khác nhau trên Internet.

Dưới đây là những gì tôi có thể làm để hỗ trợ bạn:

### 1. Tìm kiếm & Cập nhật thông tin (Web & Tin tức)
*   **Tìm kiếm Internet (`lookup`):** Tra cứu thông tin tổng hợp hoặc tin tức mới nhất về bất kỳ chủ đề nào (công nghệ, kinh tế, đời sống...).
*   **Đọc nội dung chi tiết (`fetch`):** Truy cập trực tiếp vào một đường link URL cụ thể để đọc và phân tích nội dung bài viết, trang web mà bạn cung cấp.

### 2. Theo dõi Mạng xã hội (X/Twitter)
*   **Tìm kiếm xu hướng (`social_search`):** Tìm kiếm các bài đăng, thảo luận hoặc xu hướng đang diễn ra trên Twitter/X theo từ khóa hoặc chủ đề.
*   **Theo dõi tài khoản (`timeline`):** Lấy các bài đăng mới nhất từ một tài khoản Twitter cụ thể (ví dụ: Elon Musk, Sam Altman...) khi bạn cung cấp tên tài khoản của họ.

### 3. Nghiên cứu Khoa học (arXiv)
*   **Tìm kiếm bài báo khoa học (`papers`):** Tra cứu các công trình nghiên cứu, bài báo khoa học trên cơ sở dữ liệu arXiv về các lĩnh vực như Trí tuệ nhân tạo (AI), Vật lý, Toán học, Khoa học máy tính...
*   **Đọc hiểu chuyên sâu (`paper_text`):** Trích xuất và đọc nội dung chi tiết từ các bài báo khoa học để giải thích hoặc tóm tắt cho bạn.

### 4. Xử lý & Trình bày thông tin
*   **Tóm tắt nội dung (`summarize`):** Cô đọng các văn bản dài, bài báo hoặc tài liệu thành các ý chính (bullet points) ngắn gọn, súc tích bằng tiếng Việt hoặc tiếng Anh.
*   **Định dạng báo cáo (`format`):** Thiết kế và trình bày thông tin thu thập được thành các bản tin, báo cáo chuyên nghiệp hoặc chuỗi bài viết (thread) theo các mẫu có sẵn.

### 5. Gửi báo cáo & Tương tác
*   **Gửi tin nhắn (`send`):** Gửi trực tiếp các báo cáo hoặc nội dung đã tổng hợp lên kênh Telegram (tôi sẽ luôn hỏi xin xác nhận của bạn trước khi gửi).
*   **Làm rõ thông tin (`clarify`):** Chủ động hỏi lại bạn để làm rõ yêu cầu (như xin link URL, tên tài khoản Twitter hoặc xác nhận gửi tin) nhằm đảm bảo kết quả chính xác nhất.

---

**Bạn muốn tôi hỗ trợ tìm kiếm thông tin, tóm tắt một bài viết hay nghiên cứu về chủ đề gì hôm nay?** Hãy đưa ra yêu cầu của bạn nhé!

items.title: An AI data center is being built on my grandma's garden
items.summary: In his recent encyclical, Magnifica Humanitas, Pope Leo lifts up the concern of human dignity in light of increasing technological advances. He states that we are facing a decision; either to create a world where "the dignity of every person is safeguarded [and] justice is promoted" or to create an "inhumane and more unjust world." He goes on to directly confront AI and caution us to realize that "technological innovations, including artificial intelligence, are not neutral, for they can either [...] He also reminds us to think of the physical impact of utilizing AI while reminding us that data centers are not neutral. He states: "Current AI systems require enormous amounts of energy and water … which requires an extensive network of machines, cables, data centers and energy-intensive infrastructure … It is essential to develop more sustainable technological solutions." [...] It’s hard to describe the feeling I have, deep in my gut, when I think about what is happening to the land. Concrete is being poured over what was once farmland. Land once traveled by bicyclists and monarch butterflies alike is becoming a place to store data and help train AI. The noise and light pollution is disrupting residents, and animals are being forced to find new places to traverse.

items.title: Employees at the world’s biggest AI companies are calling for a slowdown in AI development
items.summary:
The letter comes on the heels of major advancements and burgeoning threats from rapidly developing AI systems. OpenAI disclosed last week that two of its test models escaped a lab environment, bypassed its systems to gain access to the open internet and hacked a different company’s internal system. [...] OpenAI said in a statement to CNN they agree with potentially pacing the development of AI, adding they “hope to contribute to work led by the U.S. government, alongside other labs” on the topic.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman suggested it may be time to slow down AI development in a podcast interview Tuesday. The OpenAI models that broke out of their test environment are fueling “long term questions” about how AI companies should address this new rate of progress. [...] “[T]here is a real risk that capability development rapidly accelerates beyond our ability to understand or control the resulting systems,” the signees said. “To realize AI’s potential, industry, government, and society at large may need the option to buy time to address emerging risks, develop security measures, and strengthen oversight.”

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg Blasts Centralization of A.I. Power
items.summary: Technologists like Dario Amodei, the chief executive of Anthropic, and Sam Altman, the chief executive of OpenAI, have said some of today’s leading A.I. models are too dangerous to be shared and developed without tight controls. But Microsoft, Nvidia, Google and Meta have disagreed, contending that many A.I. models must be developed largely in the open for people to advance the technology and build new businesses. items.title: What makes TRON easy to share with new users? Start with AI agent payments, then follow how the rest of the ecosystem co
items.summary:
What makes TRON easy to share with new users? Start with AI agent payments, then follow how the rest of the ecosystem connects.

Small automated payments can become expensive on a network with unpredictable costs. TRON's resource model and stablecoin liquidity make it a practical environment for testing agentic payments.

The x402 approach connects payment requests with the internet's existing HTTP structure. It gives software a way to recognize that payment is required and respond programmatically.

It also connects with DPoS governance. DPoS connects token holders with network operations. Users stake TRX, receive voting power, select representatives, and influence who helps secure and govern the chain.

Another useful angle is its stablecoin network. For many users, their first TRON transaction is a USDT transfer. That simple action often becomes the entry point to wallets, staking, DeFi, and the wider on-chain economy.

A network with real payment activity has a reason to keep operating through every phase of the market.

This is where long-term network effects start to show. More integrations make TRON easier to access, and easier access brings more activity.

That practical foundation is why TRON continues to matter in payments, stablecoins, DeFi, and the wider digital economy.

items.title: Yossi Barishev and Yonatan Rosenberg spent years advising large enterprises on identity programs and responding to major
items.summary:
Yossi Barishev and Yonatan Rosenberg spent years advising large enterprises on identity programs and responding to major cyber incidents. Now their startup, Way Security, has raised $20M in funding co-led by Insight Partners and Glilot Capital.

Enterprise IAM has unusual economics: companies buy identity software, then spend three to five times more on implementation, customization, and ongoing operations. Legacy and homegrown applications often remain outside modern controls because connecting them can require extensive manual work.

Way Security is building an AI-powered execution layer for that gap. Its agents work with existing identity providers and governance tools to extend SSO, MFA, lifecycle management, and access reviews across applications that do not support standard protocols. The company says it is already working with Fortune 500, healthcare, and financial-services customers.

Quick facts👇
● founders: Yossi Barishev; Yonatan Rosenberg
● Investors: Insight Partners; Glilot Capital

The next major IAM platform may win not by replacing the identity stack, but by turning its expensive services layer into software.

items.title: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to unde
items.summary: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to understand what you're trying to achieve, but you're too lazy to type them. In these cases I like to lean back, switch to /voice and just ramble for like 10 minutes, total mess, anything goes, full stream of consciousness. Sometimes I declare it up top, something like "switching to speech recognition sorry for any typos...". Sometimes I turn it into a small interview of a few turns. But I find that the LLMs are somehow very good at reconstructing long incoherent rambles and often their echo of your own tangle of thoughts comes out quite a bit cleaner than what you started with. The result is that you improve the mind meld and have to correct things less from that point on.

items.title: How OpenAI Lost Control of an AI Model—and What ...
items.summary:
OpenAI was evaluating its artificial intelligence models’ ability to exploit vulnerable software when instead the models hacked the infrastructure surrounding the test, broke containment, and attacked a real company, OpenAI revealed on July 21. Observers say this is the first real-world instance of AI doing something researchers have long worried about: a loss-of-control scenario. If the industry fails to learn from it, it is unlikely to be the last. [...] OpenAI did not respond to TIME’s request for comment, but has said it has partnered with Hugging Face to conduct a thorough investigation and will share more details once complete. But perhaps more worryingly, OpenAI is not legally compelled to disclose the incident in the first place. [...] # What happened?

On July 16, Hugging Face said it had been hit by an unusually automated cyberattack. Over the course of a weekend, AI agents carried out thousands of actions across many temporary virtual computers, moving through the company’s internal systems and shifting the infrastructure coordinating the attack between online services to keep it running. Five days later, OpenAI disclosed that its own models were responsible.
